_doc: rpg pack text that reaches the model: entry templates · section titles · mode layers (10-06)
dungeon_title: Dungeons (enter by walking to the entrance room)
combat_require_why: This round has no [dice …] check: hit / miss / damage are not yours to decide. First write [dice 1d20+modifier vs the target's DEF]why[/dice]; write the result after the engine answers, and put hp changes in ops
combat_tail: Write this round only: initiative (first round), the player's action and check, the enemies' actions and checks, damage; hp changes go in ops; a fallen enemy's hp goes to 0; the engine decides when the fight is over — do not write it. Write a round's dice in one go: several [dice …] lines at the same stop (hit, damage, the counterattack, one line each); the engine rolls them all and answers once, then you continue once — do not wait die by die.
dungeon_tail: A room's things to do / possible encounters come from the entry pack; encounters are decided by the engine from the encounter table (see # Engine messages) — do not invent enemies; when a fight starts write [combat]…[/combat].
formation: formation: the end-of-round formation as a monospace picture, one per round (optional). Positions, distances, postures (aggressive/defensive/flanking/wounded/fleeing) and cover only; no hp numbers, no outcomes (those are ops). Shown to the player as-is.
road_clear: the trouble on the road is settled; you can go on
formation_short: Each combat round writes one <formation> block: both sides' units, hp left, front / back rows.
op_patch: open schema: give any person / thing / place a property — patch <name> prop=value …; new properties are simply added to its own record (declared ones only if mutable; name, id and location cannot change — use move to send someone somewhere)
op_remove: open schema: an instance leaves the world (used up, finished) — remove <name>
op_move_to: move: who = player or a present character / NPC's name; where = a place id of this town, or a new place name (grown on the spot if the map lacks it). Write the FINAL place of this turn, not the places passed; any place in town is reachable in one turn
op_engage: v2b's relay; in v3 step ② already ran every present character in parallel, so the world side never writes it
op_need: request: a present character must answer before you can go on; at most two per turn
op_new_location: new place (writer): new_location <name> plus where it sits in the map's tree — near=<A>[,<B>] same layer, beside them; between=<A>,<B> on the road between; in=<A> inside A (one layer down, entered only through A); over=<A>,<B> wrapping places of one layer (one layer up, e.g. a district). Unsure: leave it out — it hangs beside the player and is placed from the prose after the turn
op_link: a new path: link <place A> <place B> (two places of one town not yet connected, e.g. a shortcut found)
op_unlink: a path is cut: unlink <place A> <place B> (bridge down, road sealed; refused if it would cut a part of town off)
op_new_town: new town (writer): when the player heads for a town the world map does not have yet, the world grows it — new_town <name> from=<town the road starts at> days=<days on the road> summary=<one line> tags=<road tags, comma-separated>; then travel there as usual
op_new: a new instance of a registered class (only when the pack lists registrable classes)
op_write: file: create or replace a .json / .md / .txt in the world folder — [~write path]content[/write] (JSON must parse; paths relative to the world folder)
op_edit: file: set keys in a JSON file — edit <path> key=value … (dots nest; new keys are added)
op_rm: file: delete a file — rm <path> (only what was made in play or lives in the open-schema folder)
op_rmdir: folder: delete one made in play (with its files) — rmdir <path>
op_define: open schema: when the world needs a kind of thing it does not have yet, define it on the spot — define class <name> <title> prop=type … (int/str/bool/list, choices a|b|c) mutable=props,… (effect=yes: a state that runs each turn); define var <name> <type> <initial> min= max=. Usable at once with new / patch / remove / the variable
op_mood: a character's mood; for the soul side's SoulPatch only, the world side never writes it
op_roll: request: dice as 1d6 / 2d10 / 2d6+1; never invent the number
op_dice: check: [dice 1d20+2 vs 12]what is tested and why[/dice]; the engine returns the number and pass/fail
op_map: map: [~map] — the engine draws the current place from real state (town / dungeon / road) straight to the player; not awaited, keep writing; never draw maps yourself
op_sheet: sheet: [~sheet] — the engine shows the player's stats / pack / purse as a panel; not awaited; never read numbers into the prose
op_referee: ask the rules referee: [referee what the player attempts]; it rules on rules + sheet, you write by the ruling
op_combat: an exchange of blows: [combat bandit×5 boss×1]what each one does this beat (who strikes whom, guards, runs)[/combat]; the combat layer settles this round by the rules (the engine rolls hit / damage and takes the hp), then you go on from its reply; still fighting next beat = call it again; name×count = the other side's roster (not needed once the fight is under way)
op_end_combat: written by the engine: the fight is over (every foe down or fled = won / the player left = fled); neither the narrator nor the combat layer writes it
